b:
The small round pottu,
the hair parted down the middle,
the captivating eyes,
that smile that never forgot to open wide:
could I ever
forget them?

When I grew proud
of the sole right of the one
who took as her son
a boy who had not lost his childishness,
they mocked me

Before me
and after me,
a thousand sons
for her

Even on the day the moon had died away
one man beheld its full glory

To the one who called it imagination
she appeared as a vision,
the mother Shiva-Shakti
come in a woman's form

For your singing,
which Tamil kissed
like a picture strung with pearls,
I must be born
in another life

With you as the god
who took my hand and gave me a boon,
even Saraswati, goddess of learning,
is only a stone statue

You are the reality
that gave me
the shade called Tamil

I have even forgotten
your real name

Knowing it is no use; it is
imprinted in my heart

Even when
I am not aware of it,
on my lips
it never fades,

that
anthathi:

"Sudhakaran Miss"
note: In Sri Lanka, schoolchildren call women teachers "Miss", often joined to the husband's name, as in "Sudhakaran Miss". The moon lines recall Abhirami Bhattar, who insisted it was a full-moon night on a new-moon day, and whom the goddess vindicated by making the moon appear; he then sang the Abhirami Anthathi. An anthathi is a chain of verses in which each verse begins with the last word of the one before.
